title: When the Yearbook Turns
premise: Paloma Ishikawa, a scholarship senior at Ashgrove Academy, is surviving on grit and silence until a college essay prompt — 'Describe a truth you were forced to keep' — cracks open the school's buried history: a student death the board ruled an accident, and a hush fund paid to keep it that way. As she and her unlikely found family of misfits dig through yearbooks, ledgers, and locked archives, Paloma realizes her own scholarship was bought with someone else's erasure. In the end she publishes the truth at the cost of her place at Ashgrove, but gains a family that chose her back — and an acceptance letter earned on nothing but her own honest words.
about_author: Edmund Kavanagh is the pen name of a former boarding-school teacher who spent a decade watching institutions protect themselves instead of their students. He writes young adult fiction about kids who refuse to be quiet, and lives near the coast with two rescue dogs and an unhealthy archive of old yearbooks.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. We meet her juggling dishwashing shifts, perfect grades, and the performance of being 'fine' at elite Ashgrove Academy. A near-miss with the financial aid office establishes how fragile her position is. Emotional beat: exhaustion masked as competence.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Senior English assigns a college essay on 'a truth you were forced to keep.' Paloma writes about her mother; classmate Theo Voss reads his aloud about 'the thing in the east wing,' then goes pale when he realizes what he said. Beat: a crack in the wall of silence.

chapters.title: The Boy in the Yearbook
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Chasing Theo's slip, she finds a 2009 yearbook with one photo defaced and a name inked out: Elias Marsh. The librarian, Ms. Okonkwo, quietly warns her off. Beat: first taste of institutional menace.

chapters.title: Theo
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. His father sits on the school board; he knows more than he's said. He and Paloma form a wary alliance over stolen archive keys. Beat: reluctant trust between two people using each other.

chapters.title: The Scholarship Letter
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She discovers her aid package traces to the 'Marsh Memorial Fund' — endowed the same year Elias died. Her survival is literally funded by his erasure. Beat: guilt and fury entwined.

chapters.title: Found Family, Assembled
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. Paloma, Theo, hacker-artist Priya, and groundskeeper's kid Dez form an uneasy crew in the abandoned boathouse. Beat: warmth blooming inside conspiracy.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Stolen board minutes reveal Elias died during a hazing ritual gone wrong, ruled accidental, settled secretly with his family. Beat: horror at how casually it was handled.

chapters.title: Ms. Okonkwo's Door
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The librarian reveals she was Elias's teacher and has kept his file for fifteen years, waiting for someone brave enough. Beat: grief passed like a torch.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Voss Family
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's father, board chair Aldous Voss, probes Theo about 'rumors' and subtly threatens his college future. Beat: love revealed as leverage.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Night break-in to the records vault; they photograph settlement papers naming three current trustees. An alarm trips. Beat: adrenaline curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Consequences
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Headmaster Rourke suspends Theo for 'vandalism' and puts Paloma's scholarship 'under review.' The crew fractures under pressure. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Elias Was Real
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She tracks down Elias's sister, Naomi, who took hush money as a broke nineteen-year-old and has hated herself since. Beat: compassion complicating righteous anger.

chapters.title: Naomi's Choice
chapters.summary: Naomi's POV. Naomi agrees to go on record — if Paloma understands it will burn her own future too. Beat: solidarity across generations of the silenced.

chapters.title: Rourke's Offer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The headmaster offers full ride to any college she wants, plus her mother's medical bills covered, if she returns the files and forgets. Beat: temptation at its most human.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Shaken, Paloma nearly accepts; a fight with Theo exposes her fear that she's only ever been survivable, never lovable. Beat: lowest point, heartbreak and honesty.

chapters.title: What Found Family Means
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The crew regathers in the boathouse; Priya has mirrored everything online, Dez has the physical originals hidden, and they promise: no one decides alone. Beat: chosen family hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Founders' Day
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The board's gala celebrating Ashgrove's legacy becomes the deadline — the essay contest winners are announced there, and so, the crew decides, will be the truth. Beat: coiled anticipation.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Instead of her polished contest essay, Paloma reads Elias's story — and Naomi stands from the audience to confirm it. Beat: the climax's first detonation.

chapters.title: Voss Falls
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo publicly resigns from his father's orbit, releasing the board minutes as Aldous lunges to discredit everyone. Beat: son breaking from father, duty yielding to love.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. State investigators arrive; Rourke resigns; Paloma's scholarship is revoked as promised. She packs her dorm room strangely light. Beat: loss and liberation indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Honest Essay
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She rewrites her college essay telling the whole truth — including her complicity of silence — and mails it nowhere safe. Beat: courage without guarantee.

chapters.title: When the Yearbook Turns
chapters.summary: Epilogue, spring. Paloma, working a summer job with her found family around her, receives an acceptance letter from a state school whose admissions reader wrote one line: 'This is the truest essay we've read.' The new yearbook opens to a memorial page for Elias Marsh. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
